rule: Sports business employers with London or European offices that hire post-MBA talent into strategy, commercial, partnerships, media rights, consulting or deals roles. Covers: sports consultancies and agencies (incl. rights/deals advisers), leagues and governing bodies, clubs and teams, sports media and data, sports investors. Consulting is defined by what a firm does, not its name: any firm whose product is advice, valuation, research or analytics bought by sports teams, leagues, rights holders, broadcasters or sports investors.

strategy: Advise clubs, leagues, federations and brands on strategy, commercial growth, fan engagement and sponsorship.
media: Value and structure media rights, sponsorships and brands; advise broadcasters, streamers and investors.
analytics: Data and decision-science firms that help clubs recruit players, plan squads and manage performance.
research: Audience, sponsorship-evaluation and fan research used to price and sell rights.
deals: Advise on club and stake sales, league investments and sports financing.
generalist: Generalist firms with sports / TMT practices

Large strategy and advisory firms whose TMT, media or sports practices work on rights, valuations and deals. Client roles in those practices count, as do generalist consultant roles (the usual MBA route in); roles in unrelated practices are dropped. Firms with no public feed are linked for checking by hand.
